title: Elements
objective: After this level you can explain what an element is.
summary: An element is a substance chemistry can't split into anything simpler; its atomic number (proton count) decides which one it is. Compounds like water join elements. There are 118.

cards.headline: Everything you've ever touched is built from 118 ingredients.
cards.body: Your phone, your breakfast and the air in your lungs are all made of elements, and chemists know just 118 of them. So what earns a substance a place on that list?

cards.fact: An element can't be broken down into anything simpler by chemistry.
cards.context: Water fails that test. Pass electricity through it and it comes apart into two gases, hydrogen and oxygen. So water is a compound: a pure substance made of elements joined together. Hydrogen and oxygen can't be split any further, so they are elements. And notice the twist: water behaves nothing like either of the gases it's made from.

cards.headline: What makes gold gold
cards.body: Deep in every atom sits a nucleus holding particles called protons. The number of protons is the atom's atomic number, and it decides which element the atom is. Every atom with 1 proton is hydrogen. Every atom with 8 is oxygen. Every atom with 79 is gold. Change the count and you've changed the element. An element's whole ID card is one number.

mascot.line: One number, one identity. Elements are wonderfully easy to ID.

cards.headline: The purest stuff there is
cards.body: Remember Level 6: a pure substance always has the same composition, while a mixture can vary and be separated by physical means. Elements are pure substances, and so are compounds like water. Think of elements as an alphabet (an analogy): every compound is a word spelled with them. Water is a word spelled with just two letters, hydrogen and oxygen.

cards.headline: Elements: defined
learned: An element can't be broken down by chemistry
Atomic number (proton count) decides the element
Compounds like water are elements joined together

questions.prompt: What decides which element an atom belongs to?

options.label: The number of protons in its nucleus
Its color
options.rationale: Color depends on many things; it is not the ID card.

options.label: Whether it is a solid or a gas
options.rationale: Many elements can be solid, liquid or gas.

options.label: How heavy the sample is
options.rationale: A big lump and a tiny speck of gold are both gold.

questions.explanation: The proton count, called the atomic number, decides the element: 79 protons is always gold.

questions.prompt: Water is a pure substance. Why isn't it an element?

options.label: It is a liquid at room temperature
options.rationale: Being liquid has nothing to do with it; the test is whether chemistry can split it.

options.label: It is too common to count
It can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen
It is not made of atoms
options.rationale: Water is made of atoms, like all matter.

questions.explanation: Electricity splits water into hydrogen and oxygen, so water is a compound. Elements cannot be split further by chemistry.

questions.prompt: Level 6 sorted matter into mixtures and pure substances. Where do elements belong?

options.label: Mixtures, since filtering can separate them
options.rationale: Filtering can't split an element into anything.

options.label: Pure substances, with a fixed composition
Heterogeneous mixtures, like granite
options.rationale: Granite is a mixture of different materials.

options.label: Solutions, like salt water
options.rationale: Salt water is a mixture of salt and water.

questions.explanation: Elements, like compounds, are pure substances: they always have the same composition.
